The test image shows a corn stalk split longitudinally with completely shredded/disintegrated pale gray-white internal pith, fibrous strands remaining. This is clearly a stalk rot. Key candidates: Diplodia stalk rot (white/gray shredded pith), Charcoal stalk rot (black sclerotia), Fusarium (pink/salmon), Anthracnose stalk rot (black discoloration).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.

The Diplodia stalk rot reference (top-right panel) is nearly identical to the test image — pale gray-white shredded fibrous pith on a dark blue background. Charcoal rot typically shows dark/black pith with visible sclerotia. Let me confirm with a few more references.

None of the other candidates match — bacterial stalk rot shows field wilting, Physoderma shows dark exterior, Goss/Stewarts affect leaves.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Corn stalk split longitudinally, completely shredded pale gray-white fibrous pith
- Dark blue background (identical to Diplodia reference images)
- No black sclerotia → rules out Charcoal stalk rot
- No pink/salmon → rules out Fusarium
- No black exterior staining → rules out Anthracnose stalk rot
- The Diplodia stalk rot reference (top-right panel) is essentially identical to the test image: same pale shredded pith, same blue background, same fibrous texture
